class.name: GameplayCueNotify
class.brief_description: A gameplay cue handler with no instance of its own.
class.description: Unreal's GameplayCueNotify_Static. One resource answers every cue with its tag on every character, so it keeps no state of its own: play a sound at the target, flash its material, spawn something that looks after itself. Map a cue tag to it in a [GameplayCueTable]. For a cue that needs a node living as long as the cue is active - a fire burning on the character, a shield bubble - map the tag to a [PackedScene] instead: it is instanced under the character on [constant AbilitySystemComponent.CUE_ADDED] (its root's [code]_on_active(parameters)[/code] is called if it has one) and on [constant AbilitySystemComponent.CUE_REMOVED] its [code]_on_removed(parameters)[/code] is called - and it must free itself - or, without one, it is freed at once. An executed cue's scene is instanced too, and calls [code]_on_execute(parameters)[/code]; with a [code]location[/code] parameter it goes into the world at that point rather than under the character, and it must free itself when done. An executed scene must have [code]_on_execute[/code] and free itself; one without it is freed at once, with a warning. An execute of a cue that is already added - a periodic effect's tick - is not instanced again: it goes to the running instance's [code]_on_execute[/code], if it has one. Handlers run on every peer that hears the cue, except a dedicated server.

method.name: _on_active
method.description: A lasting cue started - once, however many sources add it.

method.name: _on_execute
method.description: A one-off cue: an instant effect, a period tick, [method AbilitySystemComponent.execute_gameplay_cue]. [param target] is the node the component hangs off.

method.name: _on_removed
method.description: A lasting cue ended - when its last source removed it.
